So, Crawley Town have made two big announcements: first, that Kevin Blackwell will be staying on as interim manager until the end of the season, and second, that the owners have released an open letter addressing fans’ concerns about the club. Here are my thoughts on both.

Kevin Blackwell staying on is the right call.

Blackwell staying at the club until the end of the season doesn’t really surprise me, as there have been plenty of signs that he would be staying a lot longer than just a couple of games.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

From the lack of news about a fresh manager, to the short-term deals the club has made for players like Connor Wickham and Ayman Benarous, those aren't the kind of signings you make for a manager who is about to leave.

Recent findings suggest that also, keeping him until the end of the season makes sense. It gives the club the stability we desperately need while also buying us time to find the right long-term permanent manager, and we have looked a lot better since he came into the club, so this feels like a good move to me.

The Owners’ Open Letter: A step in the right direction.

Sources indicate that the other big development was that the owners have released an open letter on the club website. This was much needed, as there has been silence from the club and the owners since the departures of manager Colin Kazim-Richards and director of football Erdem Konyar last month, and this has understandably frustrated a lot of fans.

In the letter, they do acknowledge that mistakes have been made, and for me, that’s a good start. They are saying the right things and it shows that the owners are listening to supporters’ concerns. But actions speak louder than words, and after so many poor decisions as of late, it will take a lot more than a letter to rebuild trust, with only time will tell whether these words are hollow or not.

Overall, I see both announcements as a step in the right direction, as they give more clarity over the team's management and more openness from the owners. Hopefully, this is a turning point, though the results and decisions that follow will show whether it truly is, and hopefully that starts on Saturday against Fleetwood.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:07.

Brighton & Hove Albion travel to the MKM Stadium to face Hull City in Sunday's gameweek 11 contest, marking the teams' first-ever Premier League meeting.

The top flight's leading scorers occupy unfamiliar territory in second place, five points behind Arsenal, and Fabian Hurzeler's men are favourites to beat a Hull side without a victory in any competition since late August.

Had Sergej Jakirovic been offered 13th place after 10 matches before the season began, he might have accepted it, given that the Tigers had spent nine years away from top-flight football.

Indeed, the promoted outfit's manager may be relieved by his team's current position, considering that last season's Championship playoff winners have not collected maximum points in nearly three months.

An opening pair of victories over Manchester United (2-0) and Coventry City (1-0) gave supporters plenty to celebrate, before the Tigers secured a creditable third consecutive clean sheet by holding Aston Villa to a goalless draw.

Since then, Hull have exited the EFL Cup and failed to win another seven top-flight matches, extending their winless sequence to eight in the league and nine across all competitions while leaving them three points clear of the relegation places.

Jakirovic can take consolation from his team's battling qualities, which have kept all their defeats narrow: they lost 2-1 to Newcastle United, 1-0 at Fulham and 1-0 at Arsenal before the international break.

Notably, the Tigers are one of four teams yet to lose at home in 2026-27, although their seven points from an available 15 fall short of the returns collected by Arsenal (15), Brighton (13) and Leeds (nine).

Hurzeler's men will be mindful of their hosts' stubbornness in front of their supporters and overall competitiveness as the second-placed side seek to extend their unbeaten run on Sunday.

The Seagulls have won three consecutive matches without conceding, including two top-flight victories that have lifted them to second in the Premier League table.

Unlike in previous seasons, Brighton's success has been built on combining their attacking fluency with defensive solidity, highlighted by six clean sheets across their last seven league matches.

The only league fixture in that sequence without a shutout was a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool, but they have since responded by beating Manchester City 1-0 at the Etihad Stadium and overcoming Brentford 2-0 at the Amex.

Having already recorded at least three consecutive top-flight victories twice in 2026, from March to April and September to October, with the latter sequence extending to four wins, Hurzeler's men now seek to achieve the feat for a third time this calendar year.

With no side collecting more points across the last six rounds, Brighton's return of 15 from 18 matching Arsenal's, the travelling supporters will back their team to triumph in this first Premier League meeting with the Tigers.

Brighton & Hove Albion Premier League form:.

Brighton & Hove Albion form (all competitions):.

Mohamed Belloumi (thigh), Nobel Mendy (knee) and Charlie Hughes (groin) are doubtful for Hull this weekend, while Matt Targett (ankle), Hidemasa Morita (muscle), Eliot Matazo (knee) and Ilyas Ansah (back) are also carrying injuries.

Matt Crooks, though, is back in contention after serving a one-match suspension against Arsenal before the break for accumulating yellow cards.

Belloumi leads Hull's scoring charts with three goals and their overall attacking returns with five direct involvements, underlining the importance of his potential recovery for Sunday; Oli McBurnie, meanwhile, has contributed two goals and as many assists to offer Jakirovic another potential match-winner.

Pascal Gross has been Brighton's standout attacking contributor, with the Germany international registering four goals and as many assists for eight direct involvements this term.

The Albion have also benefitted from the contributions of Charalampos Kostoulas, Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and Jack Hinshelwood, who have registered five, five, four and three goal involvements respectively.

Brighton's prospects could be enhanced by the returns of Pascal Struijk, Chema Andres and Jaouen Hadjam, while Yankuba Minteh (thigh) and Femi Azeez (thigh) face late fitness tests.

However, Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Evan Ferguson (ankle), Stefanos Tzimas (knee) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh) are ruled out.

Hull City possible starting lineup:.

Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud; Belloumi, Gourna-Douath, Iroegbunam, Slater; McBurnie.

Brighton & Hove Albion possible starting lineup:.

Verbruggen; Costinha, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Chema, Gross; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas.

Hull have remained competitive throughout their prolonged winless run, with their recent narrow defeat at Arsenal demonstrating that overcoming the Tigers requires patience.

Brighton have already shown they can prevail in tight away contests by winning at Man City, and Gross's creativity could provide the decisive contribution in another controlled success.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, where you are can matter as much as who you are. Banks, power grids and satellite-navigation systems all depend on knowing where a request or a signal comes from, yet claims about location are notoriously easy to fake. Spoofing and jamming attacks on satellite navigation, for example, are on the rise. Writing in Nature, Kavuri et al.1 report an experiment in which the position of a distant party is certified using the peculiar correlations between quantum particles, known as entanglement. Remarkably, the scheme’s security does not rely on trust of any quantum hardware, only on measurement statistics and the fact that nothing travels faster than light.

Carlo Pellegatti has painted a positive picture regarding AC Milan’s developments, one that puts last season’s collapse into perspective.

Rewinding to the end of May, it felt like Milan’s entire world have caved in. A 2-1 defeat at home to Cagliari – a game that they led in early on – in the final round of the season condemned the Rossoneri to a fifth-placed finish, meaning they missed out on Champions League football again.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, this is after Massimiliano Allegri had the team in a title fight going into the Spring, but ultimately the decline was near-vertical towards the end of the campaign. He paid the price for this, as did the CEO Giorgio Furlani, sporting director Igli Tare and chief scout Geoffrey Moncada.

According to recent reports, in his latest column for MilanNews, Carlo Pellegatti has put forward the notion that the defeat to the Sardinians might turn out to be a blessing. Why? Because the reset that followed on a sporting and managerial level seems to already be taking a positive shape.

“Krosche and delight! It’s a somewhat obvious joke, but it captures the expectations of AC Milan fans. When will he arrive? November 27th, as I’ve been told, or in the first ten days of December, or even – I really hope not – January 1st?” he began.

“The difference in dates for the announcement of his upcoming role is by no means insignificant, because the January transfer window becomes a crucial turning point for Milan’s fortunes, both today and in the future.

“The sooner the Head of Football sits down at Casa Milan, the better he can weave his web to strengthen the team in the winter transfer window. This should have been the job of a year ago, but was not accomplished by a shortsighted management team that never understood the difference between costs and investments.

“It’s also a shame that Igli Tare is a person who respects roles and is attentive to internal balances. He had to, and this is his great regret, bypass those who managed Milan, to speak with Gerry Cardinale and explain the importance of the arrival of a striker and a defender, who would have allowed them to be in the Champions League today.

Industry observers note that “I’m using a very bold paradox, one I’ve never admitted. If failing to qualify for the Champions League was the reason that pushed Gerry Cardinale to fire the key figures of the three worst and most disastrous years in Milan’s history, then, given the exciting future prospects, it would have been better to lose against Cagliari, which avoided prolonging the agony of our dear old AC Milan. A painful sacrifice that, I hope, will be repaid with success in the years to come.

“With a Cardinale who was too absent and distant, guilty, by his own admission, of having delegated the management of his club to unsuitable people, but who now becomes the protagonist of this new way of operating, reminiscent of the good old days.

“I obviously feel sorry for Tare and Allegri, who, despite having their responsibilities, were victims of a confusing, chaotic, and divisive situation, and through no fault of their own.

According to recent reports, “Returning to Krosche, I hope he quickly finds his feet in this Milan adventure that awaits him. I continue to believe that a highly experienced and highly skilled Italian operative, to work alongside the German director, could and can be of help to him and Milan, given the obvious difficulties of integrating into a world that is completely different from the German one.

“Gerry Cardinale and his chief assistant, Massimo Calvelli, are convinced of the wisdom of their choice, after meeting several times with Markus Krosche. I think it’s crucial that he’s not only a skilled market operator, but also a valid on-field contact for Ruben Amorim.

“The Portuguese will then be able to discuss potential choices and decisions with his Head of Football. In short, it was a position in the organisational chart that was culpably neglected, with the results that were seen, until Gerry Cardinale himself imposed Igli Tare, who, in any case, did not have an easy job.

“I mentioned Massimo Calvelli, who, in the media, always appears to be somewhat out of the spotlight. Certainly not in operational terms, because, from what I know, he was the absolute protagonist and architect of transactions that brought approximately €825m into Milan’s coffers.

“He was certainly a skilled architect of the return of Adidas as a shirt sponsor, but also a key figure in the acquisition of Generali, which will give its name to the new stadium, this time with the collaboration, it is remarked, of Paolo Scaroni.

“Therefore, he is a valuable executive who works behind the scenes, but with excellent results in terms of economic and financial aspects and also for the club’s image.”.

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 13:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 13:03.

Atletico Madrid will be aiming to avoid a third straight defeat in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Getafe on Sunday.

This is a fixture that has been played on 47 occasions throughout history, with Atletico comfortably leading the overall head-to-head record 32 victories to Getafe's five.

Getafe have been beaten in five of their last six matches against Atletico, but they do have a recent home win to their name over the Red and Whites, triumphing 2-1 in March 2025.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:34 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:49 EST, 17 November 2026.

Chelsea star Pedro Neto lost his cool while playing for Portugal in their win over Wales as he received two yellow cards in as many minutes before clashing with opposing manager Craig Bellamy.

The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.

He was first booked for a high challenge on the back of Brennan Johnson's leg – a tackle which some may argue could have been a red in itself.

One minute and 59 seconds later, he was shown his second yellow when he slid in on Johnson again. He didn't appear to make too much contact, if any, but left the Wales man sprawling to avoid it.

German referee Sven Jablonski showed no hesitation in sending Neto off, but the winger wasn't going to take it lying down.

He had to be held back by captain Bruno Fernandes as he tried to confront Johnson, and seemingly managed to shout in his direction before reluctantly making his way off the field.

Pedro Neto was sent off while playing for Portugal against Wales after two yellow cards in under two minutes.

He also had a confrontation with Wales manager Craig Bellamy (right) as he left the field of play.

Before that, though, he had a conversation with Wales boss Craig Bellamy, with officials initially trying to separate the two, with Neto looking angry.

Bellamy, though, spoke to Neto and embraced him before finally walking down the tunnel.

The 26-year-old will now serve a one-game suspension, meaning he will miss the first leg of Portugal's Nations League quarter-final, which will be played in March.

Jorge Jesus's side secured top spot in their group with the win over Wales, which was achieved by Carlos Forbs's 70th-minute goal.

Fernandes had opened the scoring for his side in the 11th minute, but David Brooks and Sorba Thomas gave Wales an unlikely lead.

That was until Neto levelled things up just before half-time, and Forbs scored the winner, with ten-man Portugal able to hold on for all three points.

Wales finished bottom of the group with one win – against Norway – and five defeats from their six matches.

Captain Ben Davies said after the game: 'We demonstrated a lot of character and we've shown good effort in these games where we've just come up short from a results perspective.

After expressing his frustration, the Chelsea star had to be directed off the field by captain Bruno Fernandes (right).

He had in fact scored for his side in the game, bringing them level before the half-time interval.

'There is a lot to take from this going into the games in March and we have to feel confident because we've been playing well.

It has been revealed that 'We know the boys up top can be so dangerous, and if teams want to come here and play man-for-man against us, we've got a lot of speed and we have to be good on the ball. That comes with risk sometimes, like you saw with the chances that they had, but I'd rather play this way and go toe-to-toe with these teams and have a go.

'We competed in the campaign and we were not a million miles off like the table might suggest. I thought we put in some very good performances, we just wished we had some better results.'.

Neto, meanwhile, will now return to his club side Chelsea ahead of a busy Christmas period.

He has started all but one Premier League game so far and has been a key player under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues will take on Leeds at Stamford Bridge this weekend as club football returns.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An early lead in our FA Trophy tie against Chertsey Town, followed by two or three very good chances, had us thinking we might be in for a comfortable afternoon. We were on top, playing well and looking the better side.

It has been revealed that then came the moment that changed everything. A rush of blood saw Nathan Laleye bring down his man. I wasn’t convinced he was the last defender, but referee James Black saw it differently and produced a red card.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Suddenly, a game we had been controlling became a battle to survive, with around 60 minutes still to play with ten men.

Steve King reorganised, sacrificing both Paul McCallum and Darren McQueen, and the boys rolled up their sleeves. Their effort, discipline and determination were outstanding.

They held out admirably until the 85th minute, when Harry Phipps, exhausted after putting in a tremendous shift, left a leg out and conceded a penalty. Chertsey converted, and you could almost feel their energy return.

They huffed and puffed, Lewis Carey made some important saves, and it looked as though we were heading for another penalty shootout.

Then came a moment of magic. A lovely move ended with Tyano Wilson slipping inside and volleying the ball into the net.

Recent findings suggest that the stadium erupted. No penalties required. Just that wonderful feeling football gives you when an afternoon of tension turns into pure joy.

What a performance from a team who had spent most of the afternoon a man short. Those are the days when you learn plenty about your players, and these boys gave us every reason to be proud.

In a recent development, our reward is a trip to Oxford City in the next round. Only five wins from Wembley. There is plenty of football to be played before we get carried away, but you’re allowed to dream. That’s what the cup is all about.

Recent findings suggest that I just wish more people had been there to see it. You can watch the highlights, but they cannot quite recreate the feeling of being in the ground when that winner went in.

Tuesday’s free-entry game against Littlehampton brought wind, rain and, sadly, a crowd of only just over 400. We dominated the first half but squandered chance after chance and somehow went in at the break at 1-1.

Credit to Littlehampton, who battled valiantly, but our quality shone through in the second half and Borough ran out convincing 6-1 winners, with Tyano Wilson taking the man-of-the-match honours.

It has been revealed that thank you to everyone who braved the weather. We had hoped a free evening of football would tempt a few more through the gates, but we really appreciate those who came. Whether you’re a regular or it was your first visit, we hope to see you again, hopefully in kinder weather.

It has been revealed that tomorrow we travel to Enfield for a clash at the top of the Isthmian Premier table. A proper six-pointer, another massive test and another chance for these boys to show what they can do.

Sources indicate that hopefully plenty of you will be there to get behind them. If you can’t make it, Bobby’s commentary will be live so you can follow every kick.

Thank you for your support. Weeks like this remind us why we love this game.

Though still unbeaten at home in league action this season, the Tigers last won when defeating Coventry on August 29 and have had to settle for a point on five occasions since.

Brighton are faring incredibly well this term with 22 points to Hull’s 11, and Jakirovic is under no illusions as to the size of the task facing his squad and also the increasingly pressing need for a long-awaited victory.

“We have to be very aggressive because they’ll come at us, they pay very intensive football,” he said.

It has been revealed that “A lot of high press chasing around the pitch. First balls, second balls, duels, it will be a demanding game and I hope we can respond.

“When I look back to Everton, Ipswich, Brentford, maybe we should have won two or three of those games but also we were down at Everton so at least we avoided defeat.

“That is always positive but we are very aware we lack some points and you cannot play all the time to just draw, draw, draw.

“It’s not enough, we need to take more risks on the pitch to try to win those games.”.

Albion boss Hurzeler is keen to continue their impressive start to the season but expects a tough contest at Hull.

“First of all, I think they do an impressive job, “ mentioned the German. “They had a brilliant start into the Premier League.

It has been revealed that “They are very structured, also against Arsenal I think Arsenal suffered. They didn't create a lot of big chances, and therefore we need to be patient because we know also that Hull is really good in transition.

“They also have individual quality in their team. Very well-structured, very well-organised, good in transition, good in set pieces, and I think it's not an easy place to go to.”.

Breaking: Hull City vs. Brighton: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.
  • Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.
  • Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.

Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.

Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.

Conversely, the Seagulls arrive full of confidence after recording consecutive top-flight wins over Manchester City and Brentford, boasting six clean sheets across their last seven league outings.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Hull and Brighton.

Nearly 67 years have passed since Hull City and Brighton & Hove Albion first locked horns - a November 1959 Division Two clash that ended in a 3-1 victory for the Tigers - and there have now been 51 competitive meetings between the two clubs in all competitions.

The Seagulls hold the bragging rights when it comes to overall victories with 22, while Hull have claimed 15 wins of their own and another 14 contests have seen the spoils shared.

Remarkably, none of those 51 encounters have taken place in the Premier League, with every previous battle arriving in the Football League or the FA Cup, and the two sides have not crossed paths since a goalless Championship stalemate in East Yorkshire in February 2016.

Recent clashes between the pair have been notably tight, low-scoring affairs, with none of their last nine meetings across all competitions settled by more than a single goal and three ending 0-0.

During the 2015-16 campaign, both clubs collected a narrow 1-0 victory on home soil - Brighton prevailing in the Championship in September 2015 before Hull gained revenge in the FA Cup four months later - prior to that goalless draw in February.

Indeed, home advantage has heavily dictated this fixture in the modern era, as Hull are unbeaten in their last six home games against Brighton across all competitions - winning four and keeping five clean sheets - since suffering a 2-0 Division Three defeat in October 2000.

Conversely, the Tigers have endured a miserable record on the South Coast, failing to win any of their last 22 visits to Brighton since recording their sole away triumph in this fixture - a 2-1 Division Three success - way back in August 1965.

Brighton built much of their overall head-to-head lead during a dominant spell in the late 1980s and 1990s, rattling off four straight victories between October 1989 and April 1991 before later embarking on a nine-match unbeaten run from April 1993 to December 1996.

That sequence included the Seagulls' biggest-ever win in this matchup, a resounding 4-0 Division Two triumph in March 1996, while they also completed a comfortable league double over Hull with 2-0 and 3-0 victories in the 2000-01 Division Three season.

Hull's most emphatic triumph came in the highest-scoring meeting between the two sides, a 5-2 Division Two victory in December 1988, while they also put three unanswered goals past Brighton in March 1997.

The two teams have also collided five times in the FA Cup, with Brighton winning the first two ties in January 1985 (1-0) and January 1986 (3-2) before Hull turned the tide by edging a 2-1 replay victory in February 2014 following a 1-1 draw and claiming that 1-0 success in January 2016.

Feb 16, 2016: Hull City 0-0 Brighton (Championship).

Jan 09, 2016: Hull City 1-0 Brighton (FA Cup).

Sep 12, 2015: Brighton 1-0 Hull City (Championship).

Feb 24, 2014: Hull City 2-1 Brighton (FA Cup).

England will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could lock horns with a familiar foe in the last four should they make it.

It will be the first time that Thomas Tuchel’s side have played the Scandinavians since the World Cup quarter-finals, where England won out 2-1 in Miami, Florida thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham after Andreas Schjelderup’s stunning opener.

The Three Lions found out their opponents in Friday’s knockout-stage draw, which took place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

Tuchel’s men finished top of Group A after a stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid last weekend.

Luis de la Fuente’s European champions, meanwhile, will take on France in their last-eight clash, with the European giants set to face off for the first time since the World Cup semi-final, where La Roja emerged 2-0 winners thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro’s goals.

The remaining two fixtures are the Netherlands against Portugal, and Belgium facing Germany.

The four quarter-finals will take place in March next year, with the winners going through to the finals in June next year.

The semi-finals were also revealed, with England on a collision course with historic rivals Germany, should the Three Lions get through Norway and Jurgen Klopp’s men beat Belgium.

The victors of Spain vs France will take on the winners between the Netherlands and Portugal.

Netherlands/Portugal vs Spain/France.

Norway/England vs Belgium/Germany.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:55 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 18:12 EST, 17 November 2026.

In the south London pub where they are readying themselves for a League One match with AFC Wimbledon, Blackpool fans who fought for their club’s heart and soul, 10 years ago, receive a message informing them that half the squad have gone down with a sickness bug so severe that the starting XI will be very unusual.

Three players are too ill to leave the team hotel, the goalkeeper selected is yet to feature in the league this season and the EFL don’t consider this predicament serious enough to cancel the game. The club are already on a run of five defeats in seven.

Moments like this reveal the Blackpool fanbase’s deep sense of perspective, born of their long and often wretched fight to kick out one of British football’s most detested owners, Owen Oyston.

‘We’re still here and we’re watching our club home and away,’ says Andy Higgins, chair of the Blackpool Supporters Trust. ‘We have a good relationship with the club,’ says his friend Dave Ragozzino, with Higgins in the Earlsfield pub. ‘The club are asking us to tell fans what’s going on, and they know we will help. Ten years ago, our club’s owners were suing us.’.

The story of the campaign which brought these fans and many more together is told in a superb new documentary The Battle for Blackpool, which screens this week, capturing its spirit, imagination and intelligence.

Sources indicate that oyston and his son Karl have both cooperated with the documentary-makers. Oyston Snr, wearing dark shades and his trademark fedora, is interviewed at his stately home in the Forest of Bowland, while his son Karl, clearly still consumed with hate and contempt for fans, is filmed clay pigeon shooting across their estate.

Blackpool fans watch their team fall to another League One defeat, at AFC Wimbledon on Saturday.

The Tangerines are just two points above the relegation zone having lost five out of their last seven league fixtures.

Their supporters fought a long and wretched battle against the club's former owner Owen Oyston (pictured in 2017).

The film’s stars are the supporters who led the fight – Christine Seddon, Tim Fielding, Ragozzino, two fans in a Mk1 tangerine Golf GTI and twin sisters of advancing years who embraced the campaign’s guerilla tactics.

Oyston Jr, who chaired the club at his mother’s request after his father was jailed for rape in 1996, tells the documentary-makers: ‘My father likes football. I didn’t.’.

It was after he’d stumbled on a managerial genius in Ian Holloway, who took the club into the Premier League for a season in 2010-11, that a full sense of the family’s greed and entitlement became clear.

The Mail on Sunday's Nick Harris revealed that Oyston Snr had paid himself £11million out of the Premier League jackpot, while critics say virtually all the club appeared to get out of promotion was a new sprinkler system. The fight against the Oystons took hold. The Blackpool Supporters Trust, then chaired by Fielding, was its strategic and political wing, flanked by the imaginative sabotage activities of the Tangerine Knights group.

A plot to smuggle tennis balls into the ground for a home match against Burnley, in April 2014, and collectively throw them on the pitch, provides one of the documentary’s many glorious sections. Fans stuffed the missiles into their pants, socks and bras.

‘I had them in my knickers,’ states Christine Atkinson, who is interviewed with her twin sister, Pauline O’Rourke. ‘I didn’t have tennis balls. I had tangerines. It was softer. Less uncomfortable!’.

Recent findings suggest that the family of Karl Oyston mocked the tennis ball protest on social media. But it was when his father began suing ordinary fans, some pensioners, for criticising him that the protest escalated.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr tells the film-makers.

‘I had tangerines in my knickers,’ indicates Pauline O'Rourke (right), who is interviewed with her twin sister, Christine Atkinson, in the documentary about Blackpool's fight to get rid of the owners.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr (pictured in 2010) tells the film-makers.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ says Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke, interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Koudellas inside the tangerine GTI, parked up on Blackpool’s South Shore – one of the film’s many wonderful touches.

Recent findings suggest that ragozzino lost his job and faced a £150,000 legal suit. Fielding, a solicitor, was told it would cost more than £250,000 to defend himself against Oyston’s legal action. The Oystons forced him to pay them £10,000 in cash and problem a public apology.

According to recent reports, karl Oyston reveals how much he revelled in the war with fans, delighting in the ‘Oyston Out’ personalised number plate his wife bought for Christmas to maintain the mockery. ‘She thought it was highly amusing. Which it was,’ he relates.

Suing elderly Blackpool fans was his father’s idea, he says. ‘But as soon as the board makes a decision, you fight to the death to support it.’.

Oyston Snr maintains he was perfectly entitled to pay himself £11m of the Premier League money. ‘Why wouldn’t we? Why shouldn’t we?’ he asks. ‘We own the organization. We’d had 25 years of pouring money down the drain without the least prospect of seeing any of it ever again.’.

It was Fielding who came up with the game-changing strategy – persuading minority shareholder Valeri Belokon to mount a successful legal challenge against the Oystons, eventually clearing the way for Simon Sadler, a Hong Kong-based financier and Blackpudlian to buy the club.

It’s not been a bed of roses these past few years. An interim club board, formed after Oyston was ousted, included Ben Hatton, later chief operating officer at Aston Villa, former Inter Milan CEO Mike Bolingbroke and Fielding. But a succession of good leaders have left.

Brett Gerrity, a one-time close friend of Sadler who persuaded him to buy the club, resigned in 2023. The two no longer get on. Ben Mansford, respected ex-CEO at Leeds and Barnsley, also unexpectedly left. Former sporting director David Downes was recently made CEO. Amid these comings and goings, Sadler has not appointed a successful manager since Neil Critchley left to assist Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa in 2022.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ indicates Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke (right), interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Coudellas inside the tangerine GTI.

Christine Seddon was a leading figure in the fight to rid Blackpool of the Oystons.

None of this has affected fans’ views of Sadler, a boyhood Blackpool fan whose investment is still giving the club a top eight budget in League One. He has spent money on upgrades to the stadium and training ground and the team’s playing surface is excellent.

Sources indicate that but his own future at Bloomfield Road is in doubt. He is on trial in Hong Kong over accusations of insider dealing linked to his former hedge fund and could face a prison sentence if convicted.

According to recent reports, that would mean him failing the EFL Owners’ and Directors’ Test and he would seemingly have to sell. The verdict in that case is expected next February. Sadler, who has pleaded not guilty to the charges, has revealed little of any contingencies he might have made. He is thought to be prepared to sell the club, though only if the buyer will be a true custodian.

‘He’s acutely aware of not putting Blackpool right back where it was with Oyston,’ indicates one source.

‘The club is so much better and professional than it used to be,' Seddon tells us. ‘But we are short of football business experience. We don’t have a proper board at the moment.

Sources indicate that 'Hedge fund management – our owner’s world – does not always translate well into football. It’s a steep learning curve.’.

Oyston Snr revealed in a recent interview that he wants to buy the club back and gift a majority share to fans. ‘In 2015, we suggested to him that he walk away and leave the club’s assets to the fans,’ indicates Seddon.

It has been revealed that ‘He ignored us, yet now he’s suggesting this. These are deluded ramblings. Simon Sadler would not give Oyston the time of day.’.

According to recent reports, 'When I hear some fans complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?”'.

Karl Oyston tells the documentary-makers that he has not spoken to his 92-year-old father since the family’s 32-year ownership of the club ended in 2019. Will he ever see him again, he is asked. ‘No. That ship’s sailed,’ he replies.

Blackpool, backed by a loud, strong away following, fell to a 1-0 defeat at Wimbledon and boss Ian Evatt’s job will be on the line when they face fellow-strugglers Wigan on Saturday, so the film is a particularly timely reminder of how far this club’s fans have come.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Yes, we want results to be better,’ Seddon says. ‘But when I hear some complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?” Our club became an opportunity for people who were dismantling it for their own benefit. There were times when we thought we would lose it altogether.

'But we’re now in a place where we were beginning to believe we would never be. We’re thankful for that.’.

The Battle for Blackpool will premiere in the UK on November 21 on Sky Documentaries and streaming service NOW.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could lock horns with a familiar foe in the last four should they make it.

It will be the first time that Thomas Tuchel’s side have played the Scandinavians since the World Cup quarter-finals, where England won out 2-1 in Miami, Florida thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham after Andreas Schjelderup’s stunning opener.

The Three Lions found out their opponents in Friday’s knockout-stage draw, which took place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

Tuchel’s men finished top of Group A after a stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid last weekend.

Luis de la Fuente’s European champions, meanwhile, will take on France in their last-eight clash, with the European giants set to face off for the first time since the World Cup semi-final, where La Roja emerged 2-0 winners thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro’s goals.

The remaining two fixtures are the Netherlands against Portugal, and Belgium facing Germany.

The four quarter-finals will take place in March next year, with the winners going through to the finals in June next year.

The semi-finals were also revealed, with England on a collision course with historic rivals Germany, should the Three Lions get through Norway and Jurgen Klopp’s men beat Belgium.

The victors of Spain vs France will take on the winners between the Netherlands and Portugal.

Netherlands/Portugal vs Spain/France.

Norway/England vs Belgium/Germany.

  • Arsenal have reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race to sign Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise.
  • The 24-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 2024 from Crystal Palace and has established himself as one of the finest wingers in European football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 13:41, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:10.

Arsenal have reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race to sign Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise.

The 24-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 2024 from Crystal Palace and has established himself as one of the finest wingers in European football.

The Frenchman has scored 54 goals and provided 61 assists in 122 appearances, although even those phenomenal numbers do not fully reflect what he brings to the Bayern side.

During the summer transfer window, Real Madrid were heavily linked with a move for Olise, but Bayern made it clear that the winger was not for sale at any price.

Bayern have reportedly placed a £265m valuation on Olise, who is under contract at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

However, club CEO Herbert Hainer has made it clear that no such asking price has been set for the player, whom they want to keep for many years to come.

According to Christian Falk, Arsenal are among the clubs interested in Olise, although it could prove difficult for the Gunners to prise him away from Bayern.

If Olise does decide to leave Munich, a move to La Liga could make more sense, having already experienced life in the Premier League.

There is also a significant gap between Olise's earnings and those of Harry Kane at Bayern, and the German club are expected to do everything in their power to convince the winger to sign a new contract.

Recent findings suggest that the Bild journalist remarked: "Every club has Michael Olise on their shortlist. There’s a lot of respect for Arsenal, but there are some really big players at the table, like Real Madrid.

"Olise has already played in the Premier League, so I strongly suspect a move to La Liga would be the next logical step were he to look for a move away from Munich.

It has been revealed that "That all said, Bayern Munich have proven that big personal awards like the Ballon d’Or can still be won at FC Bayern. So, that’s the hope of the club and they’ll do everything in their power to keep Olise at the Allianz Arena.".

Olise could still be tempted to stay at Bayern after seeing his club teammate Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or this year.

A move to a more competitive league could appeal to the Frenchman, while he may also want to join a club where his chances of winning the Champions League are high.

Bayern have not set an asking price for Olise and could demand a staggering fee, with paying such an amount likely to be nothing short of madness.

Arsenal arguably need a right winger who can provide reliable cover for Bukayo Saka rather than a player of Olise's calibre, who would expect to be a guaranteed starter if he made the move to the Emirates Stadium.

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

Industry observers note that an ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that that being mentioned, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

In a recent development, it was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

In a recent development, importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

Industry observers note that high point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

Low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and presently occupy the relegation spots, so it was a big blow before a big response.

Key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the upcoming coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

The 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games shows perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

Industry observers note that giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the new campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

In a recent development, position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

Looking upwards, Parma are currently top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

Industry observers note that milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

According to recent reports, high point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

Industry observers note that low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around swiftly.

Sources indicate that key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

Recent findings suggest that then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

It has been revealed that last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

Industry observers note that however, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Sources indicate that position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

Recent findings suggest that looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team currently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

Sources indicate that high point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

Low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the massive gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

Recent findings suggest that grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.
  • The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his new club.
  • With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.

The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his new club.

With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.

But his preparations for that match have already been compromised in a concerning security breach at United’s training centre, after a drone secretly recorded 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first session with the club, with footage posted on YouTube for all to see.

The drone does not appear to have entered Carrington’s airspace at any point, but footage filmed with a zoom lens shows the session in clear detail.

The YouTube channel which posted the clip followed it up with a statement claiming they had broken no laws by recording the session as the airspace around Carrington is unrestricted.

It has been revealed that no players or staff caught in the footage appeared to be aware of the fact they were being filmed. At the time of writing, the clip has accrued over 40,000 views.

The footage shows the United squad working in two groups. One was being put through a rondo on one pitch, while Pochettino led the other through what appeared to be a tactical session on another. Both groups appeared to comprise a blend of first-team and academy players.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Standard Sport.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has confirmed a quadruple injury boost for his side ahead of Sunday's blockbuster Premier League battle with Manchester United at Anfield.

The Reds have the honour of hosting Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils, in which they will endeavour to improve on a paltry record of just one win from five home matches in the 2026-27 top flight.

Liverpool maintained their excellent away form by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 before the international break, but Dominik Szoboszlai emerged as an injury worry following the Selhurst Park success.

The midfielder nevertheless joined up with Hungary for the November international break and played the full 90 in both of their Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland, supplying two assists against the former.

Szoboszlai was managing a knee problem during his time with the Magyars, but speaking to the media on Friday, Iraola affirmed that the 26-year-old will be fine for Sunday's main event.

"He's in a good place, he's playing normally, he was not even strapped today so he's fine yes," Iraola responded when asked if Szoboszlai was still being carefully looked after.

As well as confirming Szoboszlai's availability, Iraola delivered positive updates on the Dutch trio of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk.

The latter withdrew from the Netherlands squad for the November window due to an unspecified fitness problem, while Gravenberch and Frimpong were both absent from the win over Palace.

Frimpong sustained a hamstring injury against Brentford in October and has missed Liverpool's last six games in all competitions, while Gravenberch has been dealing with a minor heal fracture.

However, all three are in line to feature against old rivals Man United, as Iraola added: "If everything goes to blueprint they should be available for the game.

According to recent reports, "Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain, he's managing but he's been training the last two days. Jeremie is recovering the same. We've introduced him with the rest of the group, and Virgil is fine to go.".

Should all of Szoboszlai, Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong make the cut, Liverpool's only remaining concerns are the long-term trio of Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitike.

The latter is still a while away from making a full recovery from an Achilles injury, but Leoni and Bradley have returned to team training as they close in on returns from serious knee injuries.

Recent findings suggest that however, Iraola confirmed that neither defender will be in the squad on Sunday, adding: "The international break was the best moment to introduce them slowly, they've started doing things with the team. They are still not available, but it's very good news and I hope they can play in some weeks.".

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points from their opening 10 games, but they have won just two of their last nine matches against Man Utd.

Davis Keillor-Dunn's sale – or rather the way the Reds responded to it – is symptomatic of why home fans are so grumpy with their club, with protests against the management planned before and during the televised derby game.

In the short-term, the bigger worry is now he is in blue-and-white stripes, the Owls are belatedly starting to work out how to best use him.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Wearsider is a versatile forward, which is not always as helpful as it sounds.

It has been revealed that at Barnsley he scored 16 goals as a "false nine" last season before joining Wrexham on February’s deadline day. Swallowed up in their squad, he failed to score for the Dragons, and even though David McGoldrick stepped up to find the net in his absence, the failure to spend the fee on a replacement summed up why some home fans initiative to chant "Enough is enough" four minutes into Friday’s derby.

After bringing the 29-year-old back to South Yorkshire on loan, Henrik Pedersen used Keillor-Dunn from the right, the left and in the hole before asking him to lead the line, the job his successor Dave Challinor has earmarked for now.

Three goals in as many games, six in his last nine, suggests the Owls are starting to find the right formula.

"With Ali (Al-Hamadi) being out, he's probably the closest," notes Challinor when asked if his squad lacks a genuine 'No 9'. "Harry (Gray) I think will develop into a nine, but as an 18-year-old playing in League One, the physical part of that is always going to be tough for him.

Industry observers note that "Davo's probably a nine-and-a-half. He can play as a nine but also likes to link the play.".

Sources indicate that for those not au fait with football's trendy numbers game, a No 9 is a traditional centre-forward who leads the line, either as a targetman or playing off the shoulder of the last defender. A 'ten' plays in the hole behind, and a "false nine" or "nine-and-a-half" flits between the two, as Harry Kane does for England.

And although Challinor spoke after Saturday's 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle about the need for Keillor-Dunn to get into positions to score proper striker's goals, as he did that day, it does not mean shackling him at the top of the pitch.

In a recent development, "I'm okay with him dropping off," he insists. "The key thing is that when the ball is in certain areas, he gets in the right areas. If the ball is in a wide area, he's a box finisher.

It has been revealed that "I've shown him all his goals over the last three years and 90 per cent, 95 per cent, are within the width of the posts in the 18-yard box. If the ball is in a wide area, we want him in the box. That's where he'll finish.

"There's nothing to say that outside of that we don't want him working and running channels.

"As long as the majority of his stuff is in central areas and we're getting the ball to him, if he wants to impact the game in different areas, then great, but only on the odd occasion.

Recent findings suggest that "I'll go back to the Oldham game (Challinor's first as manager, in the FA Cup first round) in the first half. He spent far too much time almost as a left wing-back, which is not playing to his strengths.

"(The message was) go and get close to the goal, he gets a goal, he gets the same on Saturday, another couple of opportunities within that.

"We will give them freedom, but freedom within the structure.".

According to recent reports, quite what that structure will be is a challenge for Daniel Stendel's Barnsley players. It is hard for the coach to tell them exactly how the Owls will play when, three games in, Challinor is still working it out.

Recent findings suggest that "We prepare the team for the next opponent every time," says Stendel. "But I think two different things (about Wednesday).

Sources indicate that "A new manager has come in, but the quality is the same as before. Maybe some things on the tactical side have changed. We can see some things in the video analysis.

According to recent reports, "The other thing is the situation. It's the derby, it's a night game, it's live on TV. It's a lot more than Sheffield against Barnsley and I think that makes the game so different.".

Stendel sees it as a no-lose situation for a club with no wins in their last nine League one games and one from bottom.

"The feeling against Leicester and Oxford (two draws), especially when you concede a red card (as they did early in both games), what you can expect against a top team in the league goes down from everybody and you say, 'Okay, we can only win.' The game has this feeling a little bit.

"But there's also a responsibility for Barnsley Football Club to know it is a Yorkshire derby. It's maybe the most important derby for this club.

"It can maybe help to bring energy. We can fight against them more and we can only win in this game.".

As for special prepares for DKD, "not a lot," he replies, "but it's clear he's a really good player in this league.

It has been revealed that "A lot of players know his quality in front of the goal, especially in the box. We have to look after him.

"Wednesday has a lot of quality players but he's surely a player that we have to mark.".

"I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

Recent findings suggest that "I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

When the entertaining but ultimately rather pointless Ralf Rangnick was tasked with holding the fort as manager at Manchester United five years ago, he was asked whether his much-admired style of football – the high-intensity gegenpress aped by disciples such as Jurgen Klopp – could work with a team that had Cristiano Ronaldo, 36, and Edinson Cavani, 34, in it.

It has been revealed that rangnick replied that he was certain it could. The German was, of course, proved very wrong.

It is this kind of strange, blinkered hubris that we should not expect Mauricio Pochettino to bring with him to Old Trafford.

According to recent reports, heaven knows we have seen enough of that in recent times. Ruben Amorim and his back three. Erik ten Hag and… well maybe one day we will understand what all that was supposed to be about.

But no, this will not be Pochettino. This cannot be Pochettino.

Sources indicate that this United squad is not one built for the new United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football. This is not Tottenham Hotspur 2016. It is not Kyle Walker, Toby Alderweireld, Son Heung-min and Harry Kane. It is not physical and youthful and energetic.

Mauricio Pochettino is waving goodbye to the US national team and hello to Man United this week. But he faces a daunting task at Old Trafford.

This United squad is not one built for the new United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football.

That is why Pochettino’s battle – at least for the remainder of this season – will be about hearts and minds as much as it is about anything revolutionary that he can bring to bear on the training fields of Carrington.

The good news for those hoping for quick improvement is that Pochettino – at least the one who took Spurs to a Champions League final in 2019 and to within a sniff of a Premier League title a few years earlier – is adept at the mental and emotional side of football. It is upon this that, initially at least, he may wish to rely.

In a recent development, son told me about this when we sat down to look back on his career in England. He was prolific under Pochettino, a scorer of 75 goals in four-and-a-half seasons under the Argentine. But it was not always like that. Once – just like several current players at United – he was disaffected and unhappy.

‘Mauricio turned me round and it wasn’t about football,’ Son told me. ‘It was about me as a person and how he made he feel.

‘I needed help, basically. And he gave me it.

It has been revealed that 'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words. It was unbelievable.

‘Sometimes he had been my coach and sometimes he had been like my family.’.

Pochettino inherits a jigsaw puzzle with the wrong-shaped pieces at Old Trafford. It’s a squad put together for and by six different managers.

Pochettino will want to improve the fitness levels at United and his intense methods might feel like an ice bath to their players.

In a recent development, 'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words,' notes Son Heung-min of his manager at Tottenham. 'It was unbelievable... sometimes he was like my family’.

Recent findings suggest that on arrival this week, for example, he will renew acquaintances with Luke Shaw, one of his old Southampton players signed for Louis van Gaal at United back in 2014. Shaw – the club’s only real left back – is 31 now and recovering from injury.

The physical limitations of this United team were clear in the titanic but ultimately rather pitiful 4-4 draw with Aston Villa that proved to be Michael Carrick’s last game in charge just before the international break.

According to recent reports, invited back into a game they trailed 2-0, United’s front four briefly chased the life out of Villa when Unai Emery’s team were in possession. For 20 minutes, Villa could not get out of their own half.

But the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo simply could not maintain that level of exertion once the surge in adrenaline had spiked. By the time the game reached the hour mark, United were 4-2 down.

It is certain Pochettino will wish to improve some levels of fitness at United and his methods will perhaps feel like an ice bath to some of those United players who have approached the basic prerequisite of running like some kind of optional extra at times this season.

At Spurs, players were occasionally known to vomit during training. Pochettino told Harry Kane he could be the best striker in the world but not until he lost weight.

Sources indicate that six or seven years later at Chelsea, meanwhile, he punished striker Nicolas Jackson for picking up five largely needless yellow cards by ordering him to run laps of the training pitch. Jackson was only told why it was happening as he lay on the grass in a heap afterwards.

Industry observers note that pochettino took many of his principles from his compatriot and former manager Marcelo Bielsa whose ‘Murderball’ sessions eventually arrived in England during his spell at Leeds United eight years ago. The stated aim is simple.

The likes of Bruno Fernandes (centre) have struggled to maintain the physicality Pochettino will demand across 90 minutes in games this season.

Pochettino took many of his principles from his compatriot and former manager Marcelo Bielsa.

‘With Mauricio, there is no hiding,’ noted former Southampton midfielder Adam Lallana on the Rest Is Football podcast.

‘Everything is high-intensity, pressing from the front, and repeating sprints again and again in training so that it becomes automatic on a Saturday.’.

Trawl through Pochettino’s time as a frontline coach and the testimonies of unstinting, high-intensity work are strikingly similar. There has been no great change in the belief, even when he arrived in America to coach the US national team ahead of this summer’s World Cup.

According to recent reports, 'He brings that club intensity into the national team environment,’ claims Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie. ‘You immediately feel the tempo he expects.’.

In a recent development, for this to work well, a coach needs two things. A pre-season in which to embed that specific kind of fitness and a squad assembled to play that way.

At United, Pochettino has neither so we can expect it to be a slow burn. He is approaching the busiest period of the playing schedule – his team will play 12 games in the next six and a half weeks – and has immobile central defenders, full backs with limitations and a midfield unit that lacks legs when compared to the best in the Premier League and Europe.

Sources indicate that equally, Pochettino arrives back in a Premier League where many teams now trade off the same high-press principles that were once rather latest. Ten years ago, it was Klopp’s Liverpool. Now it’s Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton and many, many others.

Every player has a brain and a mind, though, and it is here that Pochettino will in all likelihood seek to make the greatest gains ahead of Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and beyond.

Pochettino arrives back in a Premier League where many teams now trade off the same high-press principles that were once rather new when he landed at Southampton in 2013.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino can be blunt with players. He told Harry Kane he could be the best striker in the world but not until he lost weight.

Recent findings suggest that there is not a United manager since the end of the Sir Alex Ferguson era who has not run into trouble with individual players at some point. Ten Hag with Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho and Raphael Varane. Amorim with Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo. Carrick with his captain, Fernandes.

This, as much as anything, is what has held United back this season. United do not have a squad fit to win the league but that it sits in the bottom three claims everything for the way Carrick and his coaching staff failed at their side of the deal.

Pochettino’s friendship with Ferguson is more than a decade old and endures. Ferguson will be thrilled at the appointment. Indeed, there are similarities to be found between the two. Pochettino, for example, is a small details man, a coach who understands that mood and motivation and cohesion can be just as important as tactics or indeed anything the opposition can bring on a Saturday afternoon.

Having reached out yesterday to a former Southampton player for input on his ex-manager’s methods, the former international gave an insight – albeit unwittingly – into the kind of loyalty Pochettino can inspire.

‘We need to let him integrate at United his own way,’ came the reply. ‘I don’t think he needs us talking about his secrets.’.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino can be blunt with players. He was with Son. He was with Kane.

Industry observers note that ‘He remarked, “You need to do this and this and that’s why you’re not in the squad”,’ Kane once told Daily Mail Sport. ‘And it just hit me. This is what I’ve got to do.’.

It has been revealed that equally, the 54-year-old trades in subtlety. At Tottenham, he would sit at the entrance to the training ground canteen to gauge his players’ state of mind as they walked in. He had staff video them at training and wondered why they always looked happier when they walked off at the end.

At Tottenham, Pochettino would sit at the entrance to the training ground canteen to gauge his players’ state of mind as they walked in.

Pochettino’s friendship with Sir Alex Ferguson is more than a decade old and endures. Ferguson will be thrilled at the appointment.

As strange as it sounds, Pochettino chose the detergent in the washing room as he believed the smell of the first team kit was crucial. He dropped a player simply because he had noticed him eating stodgy food before sessions and another because he believed his choice of car to be inappropriate to his relative lowly standing in the game.

These are the kinds of things that look clever when you win and like upcoming-age bunkum when you don’t. At Spurs, Pochettino’s results spoke for him but what is critical now is what version has walked through the door at Old Trafford.

It’s true that, to a large extent, we all view him as Pochettino 2016. In the decade that has followed, there have been underwhelming spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. His attempts at making the kind of emotional connections he thrives on in Paris, for example, soon ran into a brick wall with the words ‘Neymar’ and ‘Mbappe’ written on it.

To return to the Ferguson link again, Pochettino has not previously been shy of perceived similarities.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Ferguson used to tell his players that working hard is a talent,’ he wrote in his 2017 book Brave Latest World. ‘To me, if a player doesn’t work hard for the team, he won't play. Nothing happens by chance.’.

Recent findings suggest that what manager in football doesn’t value basic endeavour? Not one but, as mutual trust and shared belief starts to wane during a run of bad results, even the basics can get lost. With this in mind and with Pochettino’s energy and charisma in the building, it’s not unrealistic to expect a latest manager bounce at Old Trafford.

His relationship with Fernandes will be crucial and the Portuguese should not expect the captaincy to be a given. At Tottenham, Pochettino gave it to his goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris.

In a recent development, pochettino knows that coaches can’t speak to players the way they used to, or indeed may wish to. A greater degree of emotional intelligence is required.

Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez - both publicly critical of the set-up at United this season - can expect private words of advice from their upcoming boss.

Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford a wiser manager for working amid the background noise at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

It has been revealed that united’s players can therefore expect WhatsApp messages at 11pm at night – sometimes including attachments of training clips – quiet words of advice or observation when passing their manager in a corridor or even a short note, serious or otherwise, left in a dressing room locker. How the likes of Fernandes, Cunha, Rashford, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez respond to all this will be key.

It has been revealed that so, too, will Pochettino’s ability or otherwise to make the best of the clunky chain of executive command that sits above him. At Tottenham, Pochettino and chairman Daniel Levy hit a sweet spot that wasn’t to last but for a time saw them so in tune they even took a horse-riding trip together. It was a synchronicity that electrified the whole football club.

Here in Manchester in 2026-27, it will feel different. At United, senior players criticise executives to the media while the fans wave green-and-gold scarves on matchday and sing unpleasant songs about not one but two different ownership groups. None of that will go away just because yet another manager is through the door.

Pochettino may feel he has some experience of such background noise from his time at PSG and indeed Chelsea. Equally, much of what happens over the course of the rest of this season and, if he is lucky, beyond will depend on his own reserves of energy, desire and self-regeneration. Does his own well remain deep enough?

The man who swept into Southampton with little-to-no English but bags of ideas and energy in January 2013 was an irresistible force of nature and he ran hot through the Premier League for a while. If he brings some of that to Old Trafford then he has a chance of making an impression at least.

But Pochettino’s take on Murderball, punishment laps and the infamous ‘Gacon’ 5km running drill he has been known to use may have to wait until the summer. United’s immediate concerns, he will find, are more about a failing culture, centring less on playing style and more on emotional substance.

Thomas Frank hopes to not repeat the gaffe of drinking from a rival’s coffee cup after he was reminded of his infamous Tottenham faux pas during his unveiling as Crystal Palace manager.

Frank, who succeeded Pierre Sage as Palace manager this week, came under heavy scrutiny during his time in charge of Spurs after being pictured drinking from an Arsenal-branded coffee cup ahead of their 3-2 defeat to Bournemouth in January.

The incident was the last straw for many Spurs supporters, who had already become disillusioned with the Dane’s style of football, and he was promptly sacked a month later after failing to win any of his next five league games.

Though Frank appeared frustrated that an honest mistake had, to his mind, been blown out of proportion, the moment became a snapshot of his disastrous spell in north London.

Since leaving Spurs, Frank has taken some time out from the game, spending time with friends and family and travelling to Australia and Japan to recharge before agreeing to succeed Pierre Sage as Palace boss.

The time off has seemingly rejuvenated the former Brentford man, and when asked about the coffee cup incident, he appeared in good spirits as he joked that it was a “fantastic story” but one that he did not wish to repeat.

“I hope not,” Frank noted when asked if there was a chance he could get caught drinking from a Brighton coffee cup, the Seagulls being one of Palace’s fiercest rivals.
