Mauricio Pochettino branded Manchester United "an amazing club" as the Argentine spoke to the media on Friday afternoon at his pre-Liverpool press conference.

Man United sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month before announcing that Pochettino had been appointed as his replacement.

The South American finished his duties with the USA before flying straight to England to begin work on Wednesday, with Man United back in action away to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

Pochettino spoke to reporters at his pre-match press conference on Friday, and he detailed the importance of being ready for the clash with Liverpool.

It has been revealed that "We are so excited to be here and I think it's an amazing club. We are happy, but at the same time, so busy. I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool," said Pochettino.

"We arrive with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy with the way we love to work.

"We have found supportive people in the club. But at the same time, we need to improve our players and find a way to perform. The identity and the culture of the club are very clear; it's a historic club with years as one of the best in the world.

In a recent development, "My first target is to sleep! But I cannot sleep, only three or four days a day. The target is to get to know the people, the staff, the players, and try to have an impact from the beginning, a positive one.

"We want to create something different and positive, to build our own way here. We feel the support from day one that we started to work. The most key thing is to think about the next action, not the past.".

Pochettino also confirmed that Bruno Fernandes would be remaining as captain of the 20-time English champions amid the speculation surrounding his future.

Fernandes had his concerns this season, and it is understood that the Portugal international has rejected the chance to sign a new deal at Old Trafford.

However, Pochettino detailed the importance of the attacker during his press conference, and he is expected to be in the starting XI against Liverpool.

"I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one. Bruno is our captain and he's a very crucial player, but all the player must feel they are important. We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone," he mentioned.

The 32-year-old has scored six goals and registered three assists in 14 appearances for Man United during the 2026-27 campaign.

The meeting, chaired by Barnsley FC Supporters Trust, included representatives from Athersley Reds, East Dene Reds, Hoyland Reds, Eaden’s Bar Reds, Manx Reds, Matchday Drinkers and the Fan Advisory Board, along with supporters active on Facebook and season-ticket holders.

Following several weeks of conversations between the trust and the club, it has been decided that Barnsley chairman Neerav Parekh will meet supporter group representatives in early December ahead of speaking to the media.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A wider fans forum, open to all supporters, will follow before the end of the season.

Concerns raised at the meeting included concerns about the long-term strategy and future of the football club and a perceived lack of transparency and communication from the club's leadership and absence of football experience in the day-to-day running of the club.

The club's recruitment strategy was also called into question alongside a decline in match-day experience and attendances.

Questions regarding the club's search for a latest chief executive officer - following the departure of Jon Flatman - were also aired alongside the skillset that the club will be looking for in terms of his permanent replacement.

Industry observers note that A trust statement read: "It was a productive meeting, constructive in spirit but challenging in discussion. Frustrations were aired openly, yet what came through just as clearly was a shared passion for Barnsley Football Club and a commitment to seeing it prosper rather than decline.

In a recent development, "Much of the discussion centred on the last four years and what the future could look like. Before it began, we set out the financial headlines from that period, so that everyone in the room was working from the same information.

"The club’s four most recent sets of accounts, covering 2021/22 to 2024/25, show a combined operating loss of £28.6 million.

"We believe shareholders have invested in the region of £22 million since 2022, and the chairman, Neerav Parekh, now holds 66.36 per cent of the club’s holding organization and 85.2 per cent of its A shares, giving him effective control.

"Some in the room acknowledged that, given those figures, removing the current ownership without a successor able to match that level of investment would pose a greater risk to the club’s future than the present situation.".

Addressing the news regarding the meeting with Parekh, the statement continued: "Whilst we look forward to that meeting, it will only be as valuable as the answers it provides.

"Before then, there is a derby to play. Sheffield Wednesday come to Oakwell on Friday night, and we ask every supporter to get behind the players.

"Let’s make sure nobody leaves the ground in any doubt about what Barnsley Football Club means to this town and to its supporters.".

Second-from-bottom Barnsley are winless in nine league matches – having taken two points from the last 27 available in League One.

The Reds have not played in the fourth tier of English football since 1978-79.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty.
  • Sources indicate that amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation.
  • Sources indicate that the initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty.

Sources indicate that amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation. The latest development comes from the Experiment Foundation, a non-profit science funding organization in Berkeley, California, which has debuted the Field Building Accelerator to cultivate ingenuity hubs around specific fields of research using small, rapidly deployed grants.

Sources indicate that the initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each. The recipients, in turn, will design their own microgrant programme to distribute up to $10,000 to researchers exploring distinct facets of the same niche scientific problem. The grants will be hosted on Experiment.com, an online platform that allows organizations to advertise and fund research projects.

“We want to create a different persona in science — the people who can chart upcoming research territory,” states David Lang, executive director of the Experiment Foundation.

According to recent reports, the accelerator programme is open to proposals that broadly target oceans, climate, toxicity, future science and conservation technology, claims Lang — reflecting the interests of its funders, including non-profit organizations such as the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation in Palo Alto, California. Prospective field builders must propose a name for the field, define its core questions and challenges, and identify at least eight researchers, laboratories or communities they would consider funding.

Industry observers note that judges will select field builders who they think are best placed to identify overlooked talent, back unproven ideas and bring like-minded researchers together. Ideally, says Lang, they will reflect diverse scientific perspectives, including early-career researchers, science journalists, science-fiction authors and venture capitalists. “There are people that build momentum in scientific fields, but they are different from the ones who are getting big publications or spinning out companies,” he says.

And, in a bid to take chances on unconventional ideas, the judges will not average scores; instead, if any of the two or three judges champions an application, it moves forward.

Industry observers note that although some might baulk at the idea that $10,000 grants are large enough to spur newly introduced research disciplines, others say it is time to experiment with new ways to distribute research funding. “If we really want to help to seed challenging, high risk, ‘who knows what will happen’ ideas, then small-scale grants are a good strategy,” says Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, a non-profit organization in Charlottesville, Virginia, that promotes transparent and reproducible science.

According to recent reports, in 2025, The Science Foundation in Seattle, Washington, organized public donations to award up to $10,000 to researchers who have a compelling ‘what if’ basic-science proposal in the areas of mathematics, physical sciences and biological sciences. The foundation revealed the second round of winners on 12 November.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.

Christian Pulisic, Pochettino's brightest pupil over the last two seasons, rose to the occasion by scoring on a gravity-defying bicycle kick in the 25th minute and 18-year-old prospect Julian Hall followed in the 43rd with a goal of his own.

But for all of the excitement on the field – where Pochettino helped rebuild the American attack with a high-intensity style – all eyes were on the manager as he embraced his team one last time.

With the 2-0 win (8-0 aggregate), the USMNT now advances to the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, but that's no longer Pochettino's concern. Instead, former American fullback and current under-23 manager Steve Cherundolo is expected to take over on an interim basis, while Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one win in the English Premier League through 10 matches this season.

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino noted after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

According to recent reports, following the win, Pochettino was scheduled to fly from northern Kentucky to Manchester aboard a private plane chartered by his new club. The quick escape offered the chance to avoid major airlines following Friday's chaotic nationwide shutdown, and perhaps a few hours' sleep for a 54-year-old starting his new job on Wednesday at Carrington Training Centre.

Pochettino spent two years with the USMNT, helping to rebuild an attack around Pulisic.

Pochettino hugs a staff member prior to the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match.

Pochettino paces along a near-empty sideline after much of his staff left for Manchester.

And Pochettino didn't proposal on traveling alone.

Outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott were expected to join Pochettino aboard the flight to Manchester, where assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

The Argentine national is replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

Mauricio Pochettino saying his final goodbyes to the USA fans as he's now gonna fly to Manchester immediately ❤️ pic.twitter.com/sCe8LCjpK5.

Pulisic, perhaps Pochettino's brightest pupil, scored on a bicycle kick in the 25th minute.

Pulisic celebrates his goal on Tuesday night in Cincinnati during the win over Haiti.

Pochettino was expected to board a flight from northern Kentucky to Manchester after the win.

Pochettino had been on something of a farewell tour in the US, where he embraced the local sports scene over his brief tenure. In between overseeing his final games with the USMNT, Pochettino was spotted at the Cincinnati Bengals' win over the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

The manager, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead before kickoff, where he mingled with Bengals special teamers such as kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow.

A night earlier, Pochettino guided the US to a 6-0 win over Haiti in Miami to give his team a safe cushion for his farewell on Tuesday in Cincinnati.

Pochettino broke down in tears as he announced his decision last week, while admitting he couldn't turn down the 'dream' job with Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino walks on the field after the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal.

American fans give Pochettino a standing ovation in Cincinnati after his farewell match.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team's headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

'I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,' he said. 'It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

'I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

'Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

'In some part it's a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

United will pay the US Soccer Federation more than $13.2 million (£10m) in compensation for Pochettino and his backroom staff.

Sources indicate that 'I never mentioned I wanted to go back in the Premier League,' Pochettino, a former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, told reporters last week. 'All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear.'.

Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one EPL win.

Mauricio Pochettino insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT.

In a recent development, pochettino put together a 23-12-2 record with the US, while 78 players earned caps for the US over his tenure. Remarkably, nine teenagers made their USMNT debuts for Pochettino, including Hall, who scored on Tuesday.

But the Americans failed to crack into the sport's upper echelon during Pochettino's brief tenure in the US. In his lone World Cup appearance with the team last summer, Pochettino guided the USMNT to the Round of 16, where the Americans fell to Belgium, 4-1.

That result was an improvement on 2018, when the US failed to qualify, but not on 2022, when then-coach Gregg Berhalter's similarly team fell short of the quarters with a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands.

Despite this, Pochettino's American players have remained largely supportive of his tenure, including Berhalter's son Sebastian, who said the outgoing coach helped him 'develop as a player and as a person.'.

Prior to Tuesday's win, Pochettino thanked American fans for the support he received over his two years with the national team.

Recent findings suggest that 'Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the fans, for all the people that was supporting us in the last two years,' Pochettino stated in a video posted on social media. 'Special, great memories of the World Cup and everything that we lived together. Always in my heart, always one of you. All the best and I wish everything good for the future.'.

Potential candidates to replace Pochettino in the US include former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and some lesser-known candidates like Cherundolo, who now guides the United States U-23 team.

'For us to win, we need to be great at a lot of things, and we need someone who cares about youth development, cares about our youth national team programs, our relationships with our clubs and the success of the federation more broadly,' US Soccer CEO JT Batson told TNT Sports on Tuesday. 'We know that is a key part of our success, and it's also a key part of how we've been able to attract great people because they get to do significant things.'.

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 14:21.

Enzo Maresca has provided the latest upgrade on the fitness of his Manchester City squad ahead of Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home to Fulham.

The Citizens enter this contest seeking to end a three-game losing run, with defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion followed by a 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol both started at the City Ground and were at fault for goal conceded in the first half before coming off at half time due to injury.

While Gvardiol has since recovered from his minor matter and represented Croatia on international duty, Guehi withdrew from the England squad with a hip problem.

However, Guehi was involved in Man City training on Thursday and is set to be available for selection against Fulham.

Clarifying Guehi’s situation following a run of error-strewn performances before his injury, Maresca noted at his press conference: “He didn't join internationally because he had a small issue against Forest, but it's not because he needs some break.”.

Fellow centre-back Abdukodir Khusanov pulled out of Uzbekistan duty after sustaining a knock in Man City’s defeat at Forest.

The 22-year-old was absent from all Man City photos and videos from Thursday’s training session and is now a doubt for the visit of Fulham this weekend.

Maresca has also confirmed that Matheus Nunes is a doubt with an unspecified matter; he previously missed three games in October with an ankle issue.

Sources indicate that "From the Forest game we still have Matheus (Nunes) and [Khusanov] that are still doubts for tomorrow, because they are still with some problems. We'll see in the next hours.".

The only confirmed injury absentee for Man City is attacker Antoine Semenyo, who is still recovering from a knee injury and is targeting a return next month.

Meanwhile, Maresca has confirmed one guaranteed starter for the match against Fulham, with goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma to continue between the sticks despite a poor run of form.

Donnarumma has kept just four clean sheets in 15 appearances across all competitions this season, conceding 23 goals in total, and his decision making in recent matches has come under question.

Sources indicate that however, Maresca continues to back his fellow Italian, telling reporters: "He has been good. I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up, but for Italy he was the Man of the Match in the game (vs. France), he made many good saves.

"We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopefully he's not going to make any more mistakes. He is going to start against Fulham.".

Man City have kept just three clean sheets in their last nine meetings with Fulham, but they have won each of their last 20 head-to-head battles across all competitions – the longest winning run against the same opponent in English football history.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage remarked when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

Recent findings suggest that “We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old mentioned. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

Recent findings suggest that “I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he said. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

According to recent reports, “It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

According to recent reports, for all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

Industry observers note that “The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage noted. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

In a recent development, “It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really vital to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

It has been revealed that all Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

With less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Sources indicate that brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Sources indicate that yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

According to recent reports, elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

Leeds United defender James Justin has warned Chelsea have talent “spilling out” as the sides prepare to meet in the Premier League.

The old rivals did battle in the Carabao Cup in September and Chelsea emerged as 6-3 victors at Stamford Bridge.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Xabi Alonso’s men are due to host Leeds again tomorrow (November 21) and Justin has made it clear a stern test lies ahead.

He told Premier League Studios, as quoted by the official Leeds website: “I feel like it will be a bit of a different side than what we faced in the League Cup tie, and we know they are a team that likes to play in the small spaces.

“They have got talent spilling out and you have to keep control of that but also try and take advantage of somewhere they might not be as tight, obviously.

“They lost their last match against Sunderland so hopefully we can look at that match and learn a few things.”.

Leeds returned to winning ways prior to the international break, defeating Chelsea’s London rivals Tottenham Hotspur 1-0.

Daniel Farke’s men may well be the underdogs but just two points separate the fifth-placed Blues and ninth-placed Whites.

Justin said: “It has been nice to rest and recharge a little bit, and work on a few things on the training pitch. We are ready to go and pick things up again.

According to recent reports, “I would say from last season we have come on leaps and bounds and the confidence that everyone has in the squad is a lot more compared to this time last season. We have still got a way to go but we have had a solid start.”.

Leeds indicated ambition with their summer transfer window recruitment, splashing out a club-record £40m on England international goalkeeper James Trafford.

They also bolstered in the centre of defence by recruiting Tarik Muharemović and Nico Elvedi, who have been partnering Justin in a back three.

England will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could lock horns with a familiar foe in the last four should they make it.

It will be the first time that Thomas Tuchel’s side have played the Scandinavians since the World Cup quarter-finals, where England won out 2-1 in Miami, Florida thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham after Andreas Schjelderup’s stunning opener.

The Three Lions found out their opponents in Friday’s knockout-stage draw, which took place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

Tuchel’s men finished top of Group A after a stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid last weekend.

Luis de la Fuente’s European champions, meanwhile, will take on France in their last-eight clash, with the European giants set to face off for the first time since the World Cup semi-final, where La Roja emerged 2-0 winners thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro’s goals.

The remaining two fixtures are the Netherlands against Portugal, and Belgium facing Germany.

The four quarter-finals will take place in March next year, with the winners going through to the finals in June next year.

The semi-finals were also revealed, with England on a collision course with historic rivals Germany, should the Three Lions get through Norway and Jurgen Klopp’s men beat Belgium.

The victors of Spain vs France will take on the winners between the Netherlands and Portugal.

Netherlands/Portugal vs Spain/France.

Norway/England vs Belgium/Germany.

Tottenham Hotspur have shared footage of Lucas Bergvall and Savio back in training ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The pair have both missed each of Spurs' last four Premier League matches, having picked up injuries ahead of October's 3-1 home victory over Coventry City.

Savio has been dealing with a muscular problem, while Bergvall has been nursing a knee injury, but Roberto De Zerbi expressed hope that the pair would return following the November international break.

De Zerbi then confirmed at his pre-game press conference that the Brazilian attacker and Swedish midfielder are fine to feature against Ipswich, as well as assuring that James Maddison is fit and ready.

However, none of Mykhaylo Mudryk, Tosin Adarabioyo or Mathys Tel will be ready just yet, as the latter is still feeling the effects of the crunching tackle from Jayden Bogle in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United two weekends ago.

"Bergvall, Maddison and Savio are back," De Zerbi stated. "Tosin and Mathys Tel no. Tosin is already okay but it is not the right moment to take any risks and Mathys Tel, we need another two or three weeks. Mudryk is not ready yet.".

With Tel sidelined for another two or three weeks, the Frenchman could miss each of Tottenham's next four matches, including the North London derby against Arsenal on December 6.

The Lilywhites will also have to cope without the attacker against Sunderland and Fulham on November 29 and December 3 respectively, and it also remains to be seen if Mudryk will be fit for those clashes after the Chelsea loanee burned bridges with a few Tottenham fans.

In a recent interview, Mudryk reflected on his yearning to join Tottenham's bitter rivals Arsenal in 2024, before Chelsea won the race to sign him from Shakhtar Donetsk.

"Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret,” Mudryk Ukrainian podcast Guest of Gordon. "Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream.

Recent findings suggest that “There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal. The attempts from my previous agent were only to earn more money. But at the time, I didn’t know about it. I only understood about the commission and all the rest later on.".

While De Zerbi admitted he could understand Tottenham fans' frustrations, he leapt to the defence of his long-term colleague, adding: "Yes I can understand but Mudryk is a good guy, a good player, he suffered a lot with the situation in the last couple of years. He has to do one thing, show on the pitch his qualities.".

Tottenham head into the weekend in 11th place in the Premier League table, just three points shy of Bournemouth in seventh spot.

Sam Winnall has conceded he “probably didn’t realise” how intense the rivalry between Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday was when he swapped the Reds for the Owls in 2017.

The now retired 35-year-old was a talismanic figure in his Barnsley days, scoring 48 goals across 155 appearances for the club.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was lured away from Oakwell in January 2017, making a controversial move to their South Yorkshire neighbours Wednesday.

The move sparked anger among Barnsley supporters and Winnall received a frosty reception when he faced the Reds as a Wednesday player.

“A lot of what happened was actually well out of my control,” he told The Star. “And I think you look back with not so much regrets from what I can control, but more so just wishing it could have happened at a different time, if I'm going to be totally honest.

Recent findings suggest that “At that time I probably didn't realise how major the rivalry was, being from somebody that didn't come from Yorkshire. There were a lot of things that went on behind closed doors that have never been disclosed.

“It was sloppy in how it was dealt with from all parties and I think there could have been a far more professional way of dealing with it.

Recent findings suggest that “And I look back on it with fond memories, actually, because I think it was a transfer that brought me a few difficulties but I came through it and came out the other side. I grew a level of resilience with what had happened. I don't look back on it with any regrets of how I acted personally.

“People do move between rival clubs. Mine was obviously at a lower level but look at Sol Campbell, Carlos Tevez, it’s football. But I do definitely look back and think it could have been done more professionally.”.

Winnall added fuel to the fire when he returned to Oakwell just months after departing, scoring in a 1-1 draw and celebrating in front of the home supporters.

According to recent reports, “It's probably been my most asked question since I've retired,” he said. “And do you know what? I look back and if I could have the chance again, I'd do exactly the same.

“That's because it had been quite a difficult time. I'd had quite a lot of stick from different fans and even some former teammates that had spoken about me in the press. I felt a little bit let down by that. I will say this, it was never meant to kind of upset or create any kind of animosity towards any of the Barnsley fans at all.”.

Barnsley and Wednesday are set to renew their rivalry in League One tonight (November 20).

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:29 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 18 November 2026.

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend (Source X/adamkearey).

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

Industry observers note that some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he noted: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

In a recent development, ‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’.

Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has remarked the club do not blueprint to sell Arsenal and Tottenham target Eli Junior Kroupi in January.

Both north London clubs have been heavily linked with a move for the French striker, who scored his first senior goal against Turkey last weekend, during the summer before he suffered a foot injury in pre-season which required surgery.

Kroupi has recently returned to fitness after more than four months out, stoking speculation that goal-shy Spurs could reignite their interest in the 20-year-old, who scored more goals than any other teenager in their debut Premier League season last term.

In an interview with The Times, though, Rose has revealed that Bournemouth do not blueprint on selling any of their star talent in January.

That also includes midfielder Alex Scott, who was the subject of two rejected bids from Chelsea over the summer and is also noted to be attracting interest from Liverpool and Premier League champions Arsenal.

“It’s not the strategy to sell someone in January,” Rose stated, though he later admitted selling players was “part of the process” for Bournemouth as they look to comply with UEFA’s squad cost rules.

“It’s not our proposal and so far there are just rumours and noises. We are quite calm, like we were in the summer and I think everything we stated was clear and the things happened the way we communicated. For us, it’s not a plan to sell someone in January.”.

After failing to win any of their first six league games, the Cherries have hit form under Rose and have won each of their last eight games in all competitions.

There were question marks early on about whether Rose could handle the step up to the Premier League.

But the highly-rated German has now firmly dismissed those suggestions, with the Dorset club sitting sit joint-second in the form table across Europe’s five major leagues, behind only Paris Saint-Germain and level with Real Madrid.

Bournemouth appear to have made a shrewd appointment in naming Rose as Andoni Iraola’s successor, but he admits it all could have been very different, with Spurs sounding him out to take over as interim manager before landing on the ill-fated appointment of Igor Tudor.

No concrete offer was made by the north Londoners, but Rose indicates there was interest from the capital and a number of other Premier League teams.

“No, they didn’t make me an offer,” Rose added.

“I was in touch with some Premier League clubs, that’s right, but it was never to speak about a real offer. I did it the same way as with Bournemouth, I tried to get to know the environment, the club, the situation and then I picked the club I felt could be the right next step for me. The other club decided to take another manager, so it’s not always just about me.”.

The red side of Bristol have won the last five of their last six league fixtures against Boro while drawing the other.

All told they have triumphed in 16 out of 28 league meetings in the 21st century, losing just six.

Kim Hellberg suffered his first defeat as Boro chief against City – who renew acquaintances with former loan goalkeeper and player-of-the-season Radek Vitek – last December in a 2-0 pre-Christmas defeat at Ashton Gate.

The reverse fixture on Teesside in March, a 1-1 draw, was far more damaging in the final analysis for Boro, who conceded a painful and needless stoppage-time equaliser at a critical juncture of the run-in when their automatic promotion credentials were placed into jeopardy.

In all competitions, the Robins have lost just once in 15 visits to the Riverside Stadium, winning on eight occasions.

Hellberg, whose high-flying side head into the game on the back of no wins – and no goals – in their past two games against Watford and Wrexham, stated: "I know that sometimes things happen in football when you face a team you haven't beaten for a long time.

It has been revealed that "Things like that happen; it's difficult to describe why. I think last season, we played some very good games against them and created a lot of opportunities and thought we maybe should have won both of them and came away with one point at the end.

"We are trying to prepare for a team who have been very strong away from home and struggling at home. But they have been one of the best sides away from home and picking up points.

"It will be a tough game like always and hopefully we can win.".

After their international exertions with USA and Australia, midfielders Sebastian Berhalter and Riley McGree only returned to full training on Friday, when Jeremy Sarmiento was also due back following his commitments with Ecuador.
